title: CUDA runtime bindings scrapbook — swap and library shadowing repro notes
content:
Goal: collect a compact timeline and minimal repro commands for the intermittent OOMs and libcuda/driver mismatch errors seen on canaries. This is a personal scratchpad — keep short commands, outputs, and hypotheses.

Background quick summary:
- Infra: Ubuntu 22.04 AMIs, mixed GPU fleet (A10G, A5000), drivers mostly 535.xx rolling out but some nodes still on 530.
- Python env: conda envs installing cudatoolkit in some spots (11.8), but many containers rely on host driver + nvidia-container-toolkit.
- Symptoms: sudden "CUDA out of memory" for small batches (~batch 2), or CUBLAS init failures during model load on fresh pods; other runs on same host succeed.
- Extra oddity: errors sometimes show libcuda symbol/version complaints after hot patching drivers or when containers mount host libs weirdly.

Chronology / breadcrumbs (local repro attempts):
- 2026-02-18 09:22 - First minimal repro on my laptop GPU (for reproduction only):
  conda create -n repro py38 python=3.8 -y
  conda activate repro
  pip install torch==1.14.0+cu118 -f https://download.pytorch.org/whl/torch_stable.html
  python -c "import torch; print(torch.cuda.is_available()); x=torch.randn(1024,1024).cuda(); print(x.sum())"
  -> Sometimes OOM immediately with CUDA error: out of memory; nvtop shows no other processes.

- 2026-02-19 11:05 - Container run trying to reproduce with host driver exposure:
  docker run --gpus all -it --rm --ipc=host --env NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES=0 --volume /usr/local/nvidia:/usr/local/nvidia:ro repro-image:dev /bin/bash
  Inside: python -c "import torch; torch.ones((1,)).cuda();"
  -> Output: RuntimeError: CUDA error: out of memory
  Check nvidia-smi: shows ~0 MiB used except for Xorg on host.

- 2026-02-20 15:30 - Reproduced driver shadowing error after copying host libs into container image (bad idea):
  cp /usr/local/nvidia/lib64/libcuda.so.1 ./app/libs/
  LD_LIBRARY_PATH=./app/libs python -c "import ctypes; ctypes.CDLL('libcuda.so.1')"
  -> OSError: libcuda.so.1: version `NVIDIA_535' not found (required by /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so)
  -> clear sign of version mismatch / symbol issues.

Quick commands I used to inspect library graph: (put here to rerun quickly)
- nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version,name,memory.total --format=csv
- ldd $(python -c "import torch; print(torch.__file__)" | sed 's/__/\n/') || ldd /usr/local/lib/python3.8/dist-packages/torch/lib/libtorch_cuda.so (manual locate)
- readelf -sW libnvidia-ml.so | grep NVIDIA_\n
- strings libcuda.so.1 | head -n 50
- LD_DEBUG=libs python -c "import torch; torch.cuda._is_available()" 2>&1 | tee ld_debug.log

Representative error snippets captured:
- CUDA OOM stack:
  RuntimeError: CUDA out of memory. Tried to allocate 256.00 MiB (GPU 0; 23.69 GiB total capacity; 23.30 GiB already allocated; 64.00 MiB free; 23.54 GiB reserved in total by PyTorch)
  -- at model init path x -> fails on first linear layer when launching on small test batch

- CUBLAS/CUDNN init failure:
  CUBLAS_STATUS_ALLOC_FAILED when calling `cublasCreate_v2`
  CUDNN_STATUS_INTERNAL_ERROR during cudnnCreate()
  (these can be the same root cause: host driver had a partial upgrade)

- libcuda mismatch: 
  ImportError: /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libnvidia-fatbinaryloader.so: undefined symbol: cuInit (or) version `NVIDIA_525' not found

Hypotheses (ranked):
1) Library shadowing / LD_LIBRARY_PATH ordering: some container images include older host libs or project-level copied libs that get picked up before system driver libs. That causes symbol/version mismatches and weird OOMs.
2) Inconsistent driver vs cuda runtime (cudatoolkit in conda) boundary: using conda cudatoolkit + host driver can be fine, but combined with custom lib copying or LD_PRELOAD can break allocation behavior.
3) NVML/NVML state stale across driver hot-swap: memory accounting shows no usage but allocator reports reserved memory — could be driver reporter bug after partial upgrade.
4) Inf narrowly hitting an allocator bug in our runtime when map/munmap pattern interleaves with CUDA context init across forked processes.
5) Container runtime (nvidia-container-toolkit / OCI mount) race when nvidia-docker is not up-to-date — some syscalls EACCES or missing symbols intermittently.

Quick experiments left to run (short checklist):
- Repro step: start a minimal container without any host libs copied (trust nvidia runtime) and run torch minimal script (A) -> see if OOM persists.
- Do ldd on libtorch_cuda.so inside container to assert all links resolved against /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu not ./app/libs.
- Test toggling CUDA_MODULE_LOADING=LAZY vs DEFAULT to see if defering module loads changes OOM.
- Run strace -f -e open,stat,openat python -c "import torch; torch.cuda.device_count()" to capture which libcuda is opened first.
- Reproduce on nodes with driver 530 and 535 to see correlation: df driver vs stable failure rate.
- Add /tmp/swapfile 8G on a problematic node and rerun a failing script to verify whether swap affects the allocator failure timing (note: this is just for ephemeral repro).

Commands to validate environment (copyable):
- dpkg -l | grep -i nvidia || apt list --installed | grep nvidia
- /sbin/modinfo nvidia | head
- cat /proc/driver/nvidia/version || nvidia-smi --query-gpu=driver_version --format=csv
- python - <<PY
import torch,sys,os
print('torch',torch.__version__)
print('cuda available',torch.cuda.is_available())
print('cuda devices',torch.cuda.device_count())
print('cudart',torch.version.cuda)
PY

Notes from last run (2026-03-09 21:12):
- Node: a10g-04 (driver 530.101), container used image: runtime:canary-2026-03-08
- Reproduced one OOM run out of 6 (non-deterministic) when running a small Llama-like model weight init.
- LD_DEBUG showed the process opened /app/libs/libcuda.so.1 before /usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/libcuda.so.1 -> confirms shadowing.
- After removing copied libs from image and relying on nvidia-container mounts, same script succeeded 6/6.

Interim mitigation ideas: (short-term)
- Bulk scan images for accidental copies of libcuda* or libnvidia* and add an image policy check (CI job).
- Ensure container entrypoint unsets LD_LIBRARY_PATH to avoid picking up app-level libs unless explicitly intended.
- For canaries: ensure driver rollouts are batched so we don't end up with mixed fleet during repro windows.

Longer-term items: (tickets to create)
- Add an OCI hook or admission policy that forbids bundling host GPU driver libs in images (INF-XXXX).
- Add a runtime-integrity check at startup: compare device driver version from /proc/driver and libcuda soname resolved by the process; warn and fail fast if mismatch.

TODOs for me:
- [ ] Run strace-based proof-of-shadowing and save artifacts (ld_open_trace.log).
- [ ] Create simple failing minimal Dockerfile that reproduces lib shadow mismatch and open a PR to runtime repo with test harness.
- [ ] Post initial findings to #eng-serving-runtime and tag infra on INF-2763.

Random notes / heuristics learned:
- "conda cudatoolkit" + host driver usually safe *if* you don't ship any libcuda*. The conda cudatoolkit provides userland runtime but depends on host driver for low-level symbols.
- LD_PRELOAD tricks to force specific libcuda are a smell; they may hide mismatches in CI but blow up in prod.
- Sometimes small differences in torch CUDA memory reporting (23.3 GiB reserved vs 23.2) can flip OOM decisions when a model's memory rounding crosses a threshold — not the root cause here but relevant for flakiness.

Attachments I'll add to the Jira: ld_debug.log (strip PII), nvidia-smi snapshots, small Dockerfile reproducer, and the failing python snippet.

If someone else picks this up: start by grepping images from the last 90 days for libcuda, libnvidia: 
  docker images --format '{{.Repository}}:{{.Tag}} {{.ID}}' | cut -d ' ' -f1 | xargs -n1 -I{} sh -c "docker run --rm {} bash -lc 'ls /app 2>/dev/null || true'" 
(not perfect — better to scan build context in CI)

End of scratchpad. Will trim and move to an internal playbook once we have a stable reproducer.
